## Test Set Metrics

These metrics were computed on the 14 held-out test months from the 2011–2018 OpenDengue SEA dataset.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Huber loss | `{python} f"{metrics['test_huber']:.4f}"` |
| MAE (log IR) | `{python} f"{metrics['test_mae']:.4f}"` |
| MSE (log IR) | `{python} f"{metrics['test_mse']:.4f}"` |
| RMSE (log IR) | `{python} f"{metrics['test_rmse']:.4f}"` |
| Best val loss | `{python} f"{metrics['best_val_loss']:.4f}"` |

## Architecture

The model is a **Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network with GRU** (STGATGRU):

- **GAT layer 1:** Spatial message passing over the admin-1 adjacency graph
- **MLP:** Node-wise feature transformation
- **GAT layer 2:** Second spatial aggregation pass
- **GRU:** Temporal sequence modelling over the sliding window
- **Linear head:** Single-step log IR prediction

Hyperparameters were tuned with 40 Optuna trials using masked Huber loss (to handle missing incidence data) on a validation set of 20% of training months.

## Bias Correction Note

When running inference on current data (post-2018), a climate delta correction is applied before features are passed to the model. The delta is computed as the difference between the AR6 SSP2-4.5 projected monthly climatology for the current year and the 2011–2018 training period climatology. This shifts current observations back into the model's training feature distribution. See [site/scripts/apply_climate_delta.py](https://github.com/chuang-lab-DMPTD-TMU/dengue-fever-EWS/blob/main/site/scripts/apply_climate_delta.py) for implementation.
